title: `st.download_button` rejects documented `io.StringIO` data
body:
## Summary

`st.download_button` documents `io.StringIO` as a supported file-like value, and the public typing tests accept it, but the runtime raises `StreamlitAPIException`. This affects both eager values and deferred callables because they share the same data conversion helper.

## Reproducible Code Example

```python
import io

import streamlit as st

st.download_button("Download", data=io.StringIO("hello"))
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Save the example as `app.py`.
2. Run `streamlit run app.py`.
3. Observe the exception while the download button is created.

## Expected Behavior

The download button is rendered and downloads `hello` as `text/plain`, matching the documented `io.StringIO` support.

## Current Behavior

Streamlit raises:

```text
streamlit.errors.StreamlitAPIException:
Invalid binary data format: <class '_io.StringIO'>
```

`convert_data_to_bytes_and_infer_mime` handles `str` and the concrete `io.TextIOWrapper`, but not `io.StringIO`. The public `DownloadButtonDataType` and typing test already accept `io.StringIO`.

## Debug info

- Streamlit version: current `develop` (`1.60.0`)
- Python version: 3.11.15
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: not applicable; the exception occurs during script execution

## Additional Information

A focused fix and regression test are available in [ShiroKSH/streamlit@e4e7da440](https://github.com/ShiroKSH/streamlit/commit/e4e7da4400646822221cbdeb9423467d0ce4264b). It reads `io.StringIO` with `getvalue()`, matching the existing `io.BytesIO` behavior without changing the stream cursor.

Validated with:

- `make check`
- `uv run pytest lib/tests/streamlit/runtime/download_data_util_test.py -q`
- `uv run pytest lib/tests/streamlit/elements/download_button_test.py -q`
- `uv run pytest lib/tests/streamlit/runtime/media_file_manager_test.py -k execute_deferred -q`

comments.body:
This is a **bug**: `st.download_button` advertises `io.StringIO` as a supported `data` value (docstring, the public `DownloadButtonDataType` alias via `TextIO`, and the `button_types.py` typing test all accept it), but passing one raises `StreamlitAPIException: Invalid binary data format: <class '_io.StringIO'>` at runtime.

The root cause is in `convert_data_to_bytes_and_infer_mime` (`lib/streamlit/runtime/download_data_util.py`). It only handles text streams via `isinstance(data, io.TextIOWrapper)`, but `io.StringIO` is a *sibling* subclass of `io.TextIOBase` — it is **not** an `io.TextIOWrapper` — so it never matches the text branch (nor any `bytes`/`io.BytesIO`/`io.RawIOBase` branch) and falls through to `raise unsupported_error`. Because both the eager and deferred (callable) code paths in `button.py` route through this same helper, `io.StringIO` fails in both cases. The reporter's linked patch fixes this by reading `io.StringIO` via `getvalue()`, mirroring the existing `io.BytesIO` handling. A broader alternative would be to match `io.TextIOBase` so any text stream is covered.

### Related Issues

- [#14159 — st.download_button generate file_name and mime from io.FileIO](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14159): Also concerns how `st.download_button` handles file-like objects and MIME inference in the same `convert_data_to_bytes_and_infer_mime` code path; both point at gaps in the supported-`io.*`-types handling.
- [#5053 — Deferred data for download button](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5053): Introduced the deferred-callable path that shares the same data-conversion helper affected by this bug.
